meta.title: 5 Stoic ways to conquer your fear

plates.query: Caspar David Friedrich figure before a dark chasm painting
marble bust of Marcus Aurelius sculpture
J. M. W. Turner light breaking through storm painting

beats.text: Five Stoic ways to face down a fear that's running your life.
One. Name it exactly. Vague dread shrinks the moment you force it into precise words.
Two. Run it to the end. What is the actual worst case — and could you survive it? Usually, yes.
Three. The fear lives in your mind, not in the thing itself. Separate the event from the story.
Four. Act while still afraid. Courage isn't the absence of fear — it's moving with it anyway.
Five. Remember Seneca: we suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
The fear of the thing is almost always heavier than the thing. Walk toward it.
